source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Antenatal Care Schedule & Household Registration
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Every pregnant woman in the community must be registered in MoH 514 and supported to attend at least 8 ANC contacts at a health facility. Contact 1 should occur within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. CHPs must track attendance and follow up missed appointments.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any confirmed pregnant woman living in the community unit.
danger_signs: Missed first contact past 16 weeks gestation
More than 6 weeks overdue for scheduled facility contact
mandated_chw_actions: Register pregnancy in MoH 514 household register
Counsel on 8-contact schedule: Contact 1 (<12w), Contact 2 (20w), Contact 3 (26w), Contact 4 (30w), Contact 5 (34w), Contact 6 (36w), Contact 7 (38w), Contact 8 (40w)
Emphasize facility delivery with skilled birth attendant
Screen for early danger signs and initiate birth preparedness plan
negative_boundaries: Do not encourage or support planned home delivery
Do not delay registration until the third trimester
Do not refer to unregistered traditional birth attendants (TBAs)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-01] ANC Booking & 8-Contact Schedule
CRITERIA: All pregnant women in the community.
ACTIONS: Register in MoH 514. Counsel on 8-contact schedule starting <12 weeks (then 20w, 26w, 30w, 34w, 36w, 38w, 40w). Promote skilled facility delivery and individual birth planning.
PROHIBITED: Do not endorse planned home delivery or traditional birth attendants.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Managing Danger Signs in Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Elevated blood pressure (systolic >= 140 mmHg or diastolic >= 90 mmHg) after 20 weeks gestation is abnormal. If accompanied by severe headache, visual disturbances, epigastric pain, or proteinuria, it is pre-eclampsia and requires immediate hospital referral.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Gestation >= 20 weeks with SBP >= 140 mmHg OR DBP >= 90 mmHg.
danger_signs: Severe persistent frontal headache not relieved by rest or simple analgesics
Visual disturbances (blurred vision, double vision, flashing lights)
Severe pain in the upper abdomen (epigastric pain) or persistent vomiting
Swelling of hands, face, or sudden excessive weight gain
Convulsions or twitching (eclampsia)
mandated_chw_actions: Initiate IMMEDIATE emergency referral to Level 4 Hospital / CEmoNC facility
Position patient comfortably on her left side to optimize placental blood flow
Assist family in organizing emergency community transport and companion
Reassure family; keep patient calm and in a quiet environment
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not prescribe or administer oral or injectable antihypertensives at home (no nifedipine, labetalol, hydralazine)
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not attempt parenteral magnesium sulfate injection
Do not administer home sedatives, herbal concoctions, or salt water remedies

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-02] Pre-Eclampsia & Hypertension
CRITERIA: GA >= 20w, BP >= 140/90 mmHg or proteinuria >= 1+.
DANGER SIGNS: Severe frontal headache, vision blur/flashes, epigastric pain, facial edema.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Refer IMMEDIATELY to Level 4 Hospital. Arrange emergency transport. Position on left side.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do NOT administer antihypertensives or sedatives. Do NOT attempt Magnesium Sulfate injection at home.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Obstetric Emergencies in the Community
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any vaginal bleeding after 20 weeks gestation is an obstetric emergency. Digital vaginal examination must NEVER be performed by a community health worker or traditional attendant as it can precipitate torrential fatal hemorrhage from placenta previa.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Any vaginal bleeding occurring after 20 weeks gestation.
danger_signs: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding (suspected placenta previa)
Severe continuous abdominal pain with dark bleeding (suspected placental abruption)
Maternal pallor, cold clammy extremities, faintness, rapid weak pulse (hypovolemic shock)
mandated_chw_actions: Arrange IMMEDIATE emergency ambulance/transport to hospital with surgical capacity
Instruct patient to lie strictly on her left side
Keep patient warm and calm
Do not give any solid food or oral fluids in case urgent emergency surgery/anesthesia is needed
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: NEVER perform digital vaginal examination (PV exam) or allow anyone to examine the cervix
Do not pack the vagina with cloth, cotton, or tampons
Do not give herbal uterine contractions or traditional medicines

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-03] Antepartum Hemorrhage (Bleeding in Late Pregnancy)
CRITERIA: Vaginal bleeding at >= 20 weeks gestation.
DANGER SIGNS: Bright red or dark bleeding, severe uterine pain, pallor, shock.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Immediate emergency hospital transfer. Keep lying on left side. Withhold oral food/drink for surgery.
ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: NEVER perform digital vaginal exam. Do NOT pack the vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Nutrition & Micronutrient Supplementation in Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: All pregnant women must take daily Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (IFAS). Pale palms, conjunctiva, or breathlessness indicates anemia. Severe pallor requires urgent referral for hemoglobin evaluation.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Pregnant woman with pale conjunctiva/palms, fatigue, or known low hemoglobin.
danger_signs: Severe pallor of palms, tongue, and nailbeds
Extreme breathlessness at rest or dizziness upon standing
Swelling of ankles and legs with rapid pulse
mandated_chw_actions: Counsel on strict daily compliance with IFAS (60mg elemental iron / 400mcg folic acid)
Educate on eating iron-rich foods (liver, meat, eggs, beans, dark green leafy vegetables) combined with citrus fruit
If severe pallor is present: refer urgently to health facility for Hb testing and blood transfusion workup
Reassure mother that dark stools are a normal, harmless side-effect of iron tablets
negative_boundaries: Do not advise taking iron tablets with tea, coffee, or milk (tannins and calcium block iron absorption)
Do not manage severe pallor at home with diet alone without hospital referral

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-04] Maternal Anemia & IFAS
CRITERIA: Pale conjunctiva/palms, fatigue, or low Hb.
DANGER SIGNS: Severe pallor, breathlessness at rest, ankle edema.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Daily IFAS compliance (iron + folic acid). Iron-rich diet with vitamin C. Refer severe pallor urgently for Hb test.
PROHIBITED: Do not take iron with tea/coffee/milk. Do not manage severe anemia at home.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Malaria Prevention and Case Management in Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Fever in pregnancy in malaria-endemic zones is an emergency due to risks of miscarriage and maternal death. IPTp-SP must be initiated starting from 13 weeks gestation, given at monthly intervals up to delivery. Bed nets must be used daily.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Pregnant woman presenting with fever (Temp >= 37.5°C) or living in malaria transmission zones.
danger_signs: High fever (>38.5°C) or persistent vomiting
Altered consciousness, convulsions, or extreme lethargy (cerebral malaria)
Jaundice or dark/black urine (hemoglobinuria)
mandated_chw_actions: Perform malaria mRDT if trained and commodities available; otherwise refer immediately for lab testing
Track and support IPTp-SP uptake: ensure 1 dose of Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) at every scheduled ANC visit from 13 weeks onwards (min 3 doses)
Confirm daily use of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Net (LLIN)
Promptly refer any pregnant woman with fever and positive RDT to health facility for supervised ACT treatment
negative_boundaries: NEVER administer IPTp-SP in the first trimester (<13 weeks gestation)
NEVER administer SP to patients taking daily Cotrimoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis (risk of severe antifolate toxicity)
Do not treat fever in pregnancy with simple paracetamol alone without facility evaluation

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-05] Malaria in Pregnancy & IPTp-SP
CRITERIA: Fever (Temp >= 37.5°C) or malaria prevention in pregnancy.
DANGER SIGNS: High fever, vomiting, convulsions, jaundice, dark urine.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Verify daily LLIN use. Track monthly IPTp-SP doses starting at 13 weeks (minimum 3 doses). Refer fever for mRDT and facility treatment.
CONTRAINDICATIONS: NEVER give SP in first trimester (<13w). NEVER give SP if taking Cotrimoxazole.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Danger Signs and Complications of Pregnancy
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Leakage of watery fluid from the birth canal before labor pains begin is premature rupture of membranes. It carries a severe risk of ascending intra-amniotic infection and cord prolapse. Urgent referral is required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Sudden gush or persistent trickling of clear or colored fluid from vagina without active labor.
danger_signs: Foul-smelling or discolored (greenish/brown) amniotic fluid
Maternal fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or chills (chorioamnionitis)
Loop of umbilical cord protruding from the vagina (cord prolapse)
Reduced or absent fetal movements
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to health facility with inpatient obstetric capability
Apply a clean dry pad to catch leakage and monitor color and odor
Record the exact time fluid leakage began
If cord prolapse is visible: place mother in knee-chest position immediately and rush to facility
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Do not perform vaginal examination (introduces lethal pathogens)
Do not advise taking tub baths or washing inside the vagina
Do not administer antibiotics at home

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-06] Premature Rupture of Membranes (PROM)
CRITERIA: Gush or continuous trickling of fluid before labor contractions.
DANGER SIGNS: Foul-smelling/green fluid, maternal fever, cord prolapse, reduced fetal movement.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Urgent facility transfer. Apply clean sanitary pad. Note leakage time. Knee-chest position if cord visible.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT perform vaginal examination. Do NOT insert anything into vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Birth Preparedness and Emergency Logistics
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: By the 28th week of gestation, every pregnant woman must have an agreed Individual Birth Plan documented in MoH 514. This includes chosen health facility, designated transport, emergency savings fund, and designated blood donor.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All pregnant women at >= 20 weeks gestation.
danger_signs: No birth plan established by 32 weeks gestation
No allocated emergency funds or lack of identified motorized transport
Intention to deliver at home or with traditional birth attendant
mandated_chw_actions: Review and record 5 components of BPCR in MoH 514: 1) Identified health facility; 2) Designated birth companion; 3) Emergency transport driver contact; 4) Emergency savings; 5) Potential compatible blood donor
Ensure essential newborn items are gathered: clean baby clothes, blankets, cap, diapers
Engage husband/partner and household decision-makers to secure financial and logistical agreement
negative_boundaries: Do not support or agree to home delivery plans
Do not rely on walking or wheelbarrows as an emergency transport plan

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-07] Individual Birth Plan (BPCR)
CRITERIA: All pregnant women (finalize by 28-32 weeks).
MANDATED ACTIONS: Complete 5-point birth plan in MoH 514: 1) Facility choice; 2) Birth companion; 3) Emergency transport contact; 4) Savings fund; 5) Potential blood donor. Gather newborn warmth kit.
PROHIBITED: Do not endorse planned home births or unverified transport arrangements.

topic: Labor Signs vs. False Labor & Facility Escort

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Normal Labor, Danger Signs, and Delivery Escort
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: True labor contractions become stronger, longer, and closer together. False labor pains are irregular and fade with walking or resting. CHPs must escort women in true labor to the health facility without delay.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman at term (>= 37 weeks) reporting lower abdominal cramping or backache.
danger_signs: Contractions occurring every 2-3 minutes with urge to push (imminent birth)
Bright red bleeding, meconium-stained fluid, or severe unrelenting pain
Labor lasting longer than 12 hours without delivery (prolonged labor)
mandated_chw_actions: Differentiate true labor (regular, tightening, increasing frequency/intensity, bloody show) from false labor (irregular, relieved by rest)
If true labor confirmed: immediately call designated transport and escort woman to facility
Carry maternal health booklet (MoH 216) and emergency contact details
Encourage calm breathing and supportive positioning during travel
negative_boundaries: Do not wait until the head is crowning to initiate travel
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer traditional labor-accelerating herbs ('kaloba' / uterine stimulants)
Do not advise prolonged pushing before reaching the health facility

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-08] Labor Signs & Facility Escort
CRITERIA: Gestation >= 37 weeks with labor contractions.
DANGER SIGNS: Contractions every 2-3 min, urge to push, vaginal bleeding, labor >12 hours.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Verify true labor (regular contractions, bloody show). Immediately activate transport and escort to facility with MoH 216 card.
PROHIBITED: Never give traditional labor herbs. Do not delay facility transfer.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Emergency Delivery Triage in Community Settings
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: If delivery is imminent and transfer is impossible, ensure clean hands and surfaces. Support the baby's head gently without pulling. Place baby skin-to-skin immediately. Never pull the umbilical cord to deliver the placenta.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Baby's head visible at vaginal opening (crowning); impossible to reach facility in time.
danger_signs: Loop of umbilical cord prolapsed ahead of head
Hand, foot, or breech presentation (malpresentation)
Retained placenta (>30 minutes after baby's birth) or severe bleeding
mandated_chw_actions: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean running water; spread clean dry cloth under mother
Support head gently as it delivers; do not pull baby
Immediately wipe baby's face, dry body thoroughly, and place skin-to-skin on mother's bare chest; cover with warm dry cloth and cap
Wait 1-3 minutes before tying cord with two clean ties (at 2cm and 5cm from abdomen) and cut with sterile blade
Encourage immediate breastfeeding; massage fundus gently after placenta delivers spontaneously
Arrange immediate post-delivery transfer of mother-baby dyad to health facility
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pull on the umbilical cord to speed delivery of placenta (causes fatal uterine inversion)
NEVER insert fingers or hands into the birth canal
Do not bathe the baby for at least 24 hours

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-09] Imminent Emergency Delivery
CRITERIA: Head crowning; delivery unavoidable before transport.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Clean hands. Support head gently (no pulling). Dry baby immediately. Skin-to-skin on mother's chest. Tie cord at 2cm and 5cm with clean ties. Cut with sterile blade. Immediate breastfeeding. Escort dyad to facility.
ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pull the cord to deliver placenta. Never insert hands into birth canal.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Postnatal Home Visit Schedule & Assessment
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: The first 48 hours after birth carry the highest risk of maternal and neonatal death. CHPs must visit the mother and baby within 24 hours of birth, followed by visits on Day 3 (48-72h), Day 7-14, and at 6 weeks.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All recently delivered mothers and newborns in the community unit.
danger_signs: No PNC contact within first 48 hours after delivery
Fever, heavy bleeding, or newborn inability to feed at any visit
mandated_chw_actions: Conduct 4 scheduled home PNC visits: Visit 1 (<24h), Visit 2 (Day 3 / 48-72h), Visit 3 (Day 7-14), Visit 4 (6 weeks)
Assess maternal vitals, uterine involution, vaginal bleeding (lochia), and emotional well-being
Assess newborn cord healing, temperature, breathing rate, color, and breastfeeding latch
Verify birth registration and confirm BCG and OPV0 immunization uptake
negative_boundaries: Do not delay the first visit beyond 48 hours post-delivery
Do not discharge a mother-baby dyad from active monitoring if danger signs are present

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-10] Postnatal Care (PNC) Schedule
CRITERIA: All recently delivered mothers and newborns.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Conduct 4 PNC visits: Visit 1 (<24h), Visit 2 (Day 3), Visit 3 (Day 7-14), Visit 4 (6 weeks). Check maternal bleeding, fever, depression; check newborn cord, breathing, temperature, and breastfeeding.
RULE: Never delay the first PNC visit beyond 48 hours.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Postpartum Emergencies in the Community
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Severe bleeding after delivery (soaking more than two sanitary pads in an hour or continuous trickle) is postpartum hemorrhage. It is the leading cause of maternal mortality. Continuous fundal massage and immediate emergency referral are required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman who has delivered within the past 6 weeks soaking >2 large pads in 1 hour or passing large clots.
danger_signs: Continuous trickling or gushing of blood from vagina
Soft, boggy uterus that does not harden on palpation
Maternal pallor, cold extremities, rapid weak pulse, dizziness, or loss of consciousness
mandated_chw_actions: ACT IMMEDIATELY: Call emergency transport for transfer to hospital with blood transfusion and surgical capacity
Perform vigorous, circular uterine fundal massage until uterus contracts into a firm, hard ball
Put newborn to breast immediately (suckling stimulates natural oxytocin release and uterine contraction)
Keep mother lying flat with legs elevated 30 cm; keep warm with blankets; do not leave unattended
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER pack the vagina with cloth, cotton, or towels (conceals internal bleeding)
NEVER give herbal remedies or sedatives
Do not stop fundal massage until uterus is firm and transfer arrives

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-11] Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)
CRITERIA: Soaking >2 pads in 1 hour, continuous bleeding, or boggy uterus.
DANGER SIGNS: Gushing blood, dizziness, pallor, rapid pulse, loss of consciousness.
MANDATED ACTIONS: EMERGENCY transfer to Level 4 Hospital. Vigorously massage uterine fundus until firm. Put baby to breast immediately. Elevate legs, keep warm.
ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Never pack vagina with cloth. Do not give herbal concoctions.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Postpartum Infections and Management
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Fever greater than 38°C occurring between delivery and 42 days postpartum, accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge and pelvic pain, is puerperal sepsis. It requires urgent hospital referral for systemic intravenous antibiotics.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Woman within 42 days of delivery presenting with fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or foul lochia.
danger_signs: Foul-smelling, purulent vaginal discharge (lochia)
Severe continuous lower abdominal or uterine tenderness
High fever with rigors, sweating, and rapid breathing
Lethargy, confusion, or drop in blood pressure (septic shock)
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to Level 4 Health Facility for clinical workup and intravenous antibiotic therapy
Encourage clean fluid intake to prevent dehydration
Instruct on hygiene: change clean pads frequently; wash hands before and after perineal care
Help arrange transport and child care for older siblings
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not treat with oral paracetamol alone without facility referral
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not douch, wash inside the vagina, or insert herbal pessaries
Do not delay referral beyond 4 hours

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-12] Puerperal Sepsis (Postpartum Infection)
CRITERIA: Postpartum fever (Temp >= 38.0°C) or foul vaginal discharge within 6 weeks.
DANGER SIGNS: Foul-smelling lochia, severe lower abdominal tenderness, chills, septic shock.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Urgent referral to Level 4 Hospital for IV antibiotics. Encourage hydration. Strict hand hygiene.
FORBIDDEN: Do not treat with simple analgesics alone. NEVER douche or wash inside vagina.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support in the Postnatal Period
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Postpartum depression and psychosis can occur within the first year after delivery. Severe depression, withdrawal, or thoughts of self-harm or harming the infant require immediate medical and psychiatric assessment.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Postpartum mother exhibiting persistent low mood, loss of interest, severe anxiety, or detachment from newborn.
danger_signs: Mother expressing thoughts of suicide or self-harm
Mother expressing thoughts or urges to harm the newborn
Disorganized speech, hearing voices, extreme agitation, or confusion (postpartum psychosis)
Complete refusal to feed, touch, or care for the newborn
mandated_chw_actions: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental listening; reassure mother that depression is a treatable medical condition, not a personal failure
Engage spouse, mother-in-law, or trusted family members to take over newborn care and household duties
If self-harm or psychosis signs are present: arrange IMMEDIATE escorted facility transfer to medical/psychiatric team
Ensure the infant is never left alone unsupervised with the mother if severe detachment or psychosis is suspected
negative_boundaries: Do not dismiss symptoms as 'spiritual weakness', 'demonic possession', or laziness
Do not recommend isolation or physical restraint at home

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-13] Maternal Postpartum Mental Health
CRITERIA: Persistent sadness, crying, severe anxiety, or detachment within 1 year of birth.
DANGER SIGNS: Thoughts of self-harm or harming baby, hallucinations, hearing voices, refusal to care for infant.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Empathetic counseling. Mobilize family support for infant care. Immediate escorted referral for psychiatric evaluation if self-harm/psychosis suspected. Keep infant supervised.
PROHIBITED: Do not dismiss as spiritual weakness. Never leave infant unmonitored.

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Essential Newborn Care at Birth
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Newborn hypothermia is a silent killer. Immediate drying, direct skin-to-skin contact with the mother, and delayed bathing for at least 24 hours are vital protective interventions.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All newborns from delivery through the first 28 days of life.
danger_signs: Axillary temperature < 36.5°C (hypothermia) or cold extremities with blue lips
Baby cold to touch, sluggish, weak cry, and refusing to breastfeed
Body temperature > 37.5°C (hyperthermia or fever)
mandated_chw_actions: Immediately place newborn naked (with diaper and cap) skin-to-skin on mother's bare chest; cover both with warm dry blanket
Keep room warm (>25°C), closed, and protected from drafts
Ensure baby wears a warm hat and socks; change wet diapers immediately
Promote frequent breastfeeding every 2 hours to provide calories for thermoregulation
If temp remains < 36.5°C despite 1 hour of skin-to-skin: refer urgently to health facility
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: Do not bathe the newborn within the first 24 hours of life
NEVER use hot water bottles, charcoal jikos, or open flames near the baby (severe risk of burns and carbon monoxide poisoning)
Do not leave newborn unwrapped on cold scales or tables

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-14] Newborn Thermal Care & Hypothermia
CRITERIA: All newborns (0-28 days).
DANGER SIGNS: Axillary temp < 36.5°C, cold extremities, weak suckling, blue lips, temp > 37.5°C.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Immediate skin-to-skin contact on mother's chest. Warm hat, socks, blanket. Breastfeed every 2 hours. Refer if cold persists after 1 hour.
FORBIDDEN: Do NOT bathe within first 24 hours. NEVER use hot water bottles or charcoal jikos near baby.

topic: Cord Care with 7.1% Chlorhexidine Digluconate Gel

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Clean Cord Care and Infection Prevention
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Apply 7.1% Chlorhexidine digluconate gel to the cord stump and surrounding skin daily for the first 7 days of life. Never apply cow dung, ash, soot, cooking oil, or traditional powders to the cord.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: All newborns from birth until the umbilical cord stump separates and heals.
danger_signs: Application of animal dung, mud, ash, or unprescribed powders to the cord
Bleeding from the cord tie or cut surface
mandated_chw_actions: Teach mother clean handwashing with soap and clean water before touching the cord
Demonstrate application of 7.1% Chlorhexidine digluconate gel (delivering 4% chlorhexidine) to the cord stump, base, and around umbilicus once daily for 7 days
Keep the cord stump clean, exposed to air, and loosely covered with clean loose clothing
Fold the diaper below the umbilicus to avoid urine contamination
negative_boundaries: ABSOLUTE PROHIBITION: Do NOT apply cow dung, mud, ash, soot, saliva, breast milk, or herbal pastes to the cord
Do NOT bandage, bind, or seal the cord stump with coins or tight cloth wraps
Do not pull on the cord stump even if it is hanging by a thread

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-15] Cord Care & 7.1% Chlorhexidine
CRITERIA: Daily cord care for all newborns until healed.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Wash hands with soap. Apply 7.1% Chlorhexidine gel to cord stump and base once daily for 7 days. Keep exposed to air. Fold diaper below umbilicus.
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: NEVER apply cow dung, ash, oil, saliva, or herbs. Do NOT bandage tightly or pull stump.

topic: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for Low Birth Weight (<2.5 kg)

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Care of the Small and Low Birth Weight Newborn
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Babies born weighing less than 2,500g or born before 37 weeks require Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC). Continuous skin-to-skin contact, frequent feeding, and infection control dramatically increase survival.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Stable newborn with birth weight < 2,500g (2.5 kg) or born before 37 completed weeks.
danger_signs: Weight < 2,000g (< 2.0 kg) or inability to suckle from breast
Apneic pauses (baby stops breathing for >20 seconds or turns blue)
Persistent hypothermia (< 36.5°C) despite KMC
Loss of >10% of birth weight
mandated_chw_actions: Teach and support continuous Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC): position infant naked (cap and diaper only) upright on mother's bare chest between breasts
Secure baby with KMC binder or soft wrap; engage father or relatives to share KMC shifts
Support frequent exclusive breastfeeding or cup feeding with expressed breast milk every 2 hours
Weigh baby weekly using CHP hanging scale and track growth trajectory
Refer promptly if breathing difficulty, severe lethargy, or weight loss occurs
negative_boundaries: Do not isolate low birth weight baby in separate crib away from mother
Do not feed animal milk, infant formula, or tea
Do not use hot water bottles or warm stones

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-16] Kangaroo Mother Care (Low Birth Weight <2.5kg)
CRITERIA: Stable infant birth weight < 2,500g or preterm.
DANGER SIGNS: Weight < 2,000g, breathing pauses >20s, inability to feed, persistent hypothermia.
MANDATED ACTIONS: Continuous skin-to-skin KMC in upright chest position. Warm cap and wrap. Feed expressed milk/breastfeed every 2 hours. Weekly weight tracking.
PROHIBITED: Do not isolate baby from mother. Never give non-breastmilk liquids.

topic: Severe Neonatal Sepsis / Systemic Infection Triage

source_reference.manual: CHP Technical Training Manual - Module 2: Maternal and Newborn Health
source_reference.section: Management of Sick Newborn and Referral Danger Signs
source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Any newborn with danger signs including inability to feed, convulsions, fast breathing (>60 breaths/min), severe chest indrawing, or fever/hypothermia has severe neonatal infection and requires immediate emergency hospital admission.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Newborn (0-28 days) presenting with any general danger sign of severe illness.
danger_signs: Inability to suckle, latch, or feed at all
Convulsions, fits, or abnormal twitching of limbs
Fast breathing (respiratory rate >= 60 breaths/min on two counts)
Severe lower chest wall indrawing (deep hollows on inhalation)
Grunting on exhalation or cyanosis (blue tongue/lips)
Abnormally sleepy, lethargic, or unconscious; floppy posture
Fever (Temp > 37.5°C) or severe hypothermia (< 36.5°C not correcting)
mandated_chw_actions: MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Facilitate IMMEDIATE emergency hospital transfer to Level 4/Newborn Unit
Instruct mother to carry baby skin-to-skin under her clothing to maintain warmth during transit
If baby is able to swallow: encourage frequent sips of expressed breast milk on the way
Alert receiving facility staff in advance if communication is available
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not administer oral or injectable antibiotics at home (must be given at hospital)
STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not give cold water sponge baths to febrile newborns
Do not force-feed a convulsing or unconscious infant (risk of fatal aspiration)

prompt_injection_chunk:
### [PROTOCOL: KENYA-MOH-MNH-17] Severe Neonatal Sepsis (Danger Signs)
CRITERIA: Newborn 0-28 days with systemic danger signs.
DANGER SIGNS: Inability to feed, convulsions, fast breathing >= 60/min, chest indrawing, grunting, lethargy, fever/hypothermia.
MANDATED ACTIONS: MEDICAL EMERGENCY. Immediate transfer to hospital newborn unit. Keep skin-to-skin warm during transit. Sips of breast milk if swallowing.

source_reference.verbatim_page_excerpt: Jaundice appearing on the first day of life, or deep jaundice extending to the palms and soles at any time, is pathological. Untreated severe jaundice causes irreversible brain damage (kernicterus). Urgent referral for phototherapy is required.

clinical_payload.entry_criteria: Newborn exhibiting yellowish discoloration of the whites of eyes, face, trunk, or extremities.
danger_signs: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of birth (always pathological)

Dark urine or pale/clay-colored stools
Baby unusually sleepy, difficult to wake, arching back, or crying with high-pitched sound (kernicterus warning)
mandated_chw_actions: Refer urgently to health facility with laboratory bilirubin testing and phototherapy equipment
Encourage frequent exclusive breastfeeding (every 1.5 to 2 hours) to promote bowel movements and bilirubin excretion
Instruct family not to delay referral; explain brain toxicity risk
negative_boundaries: STRICTLY FORBIDDEN: Do not advise exposing the baby to direct burning sunlight (causes severe sunburn and dehydration without curing pathological jaundice)
Do not give glucose water, herbal concoctions, or formula feeds
Do not delay referral for jaundice extending to feet
